one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never identified the correct protein components (SNAP-tag as molecule binder, FPbase-verified 505nm/610nm fluorescent proteins as donor/acceptor) required by the task specification, instead hardcoding generic or incorrect sequences and submitting a gBlock with 192 GC-content window violations and wrong protein identities.
t_err_evidence: In step 17, the agent writes design_gblock.py with a hardcoded generic protein A/G fragment as antibody binder, the 2IB5 chromoprotein sequence as molecule binder instead of SNAP-tag, and placeholder/hardcoded fluorescent protein sequences not verified against FPbase for the required 505nm excitation / 610nm emission FRET pair. These design choices violate multiple explicit task requirements without the agent ever consulting or verifying them.
t_commit_evidence: Step 18 executes design_gblock.py and writes /app/gblock.txt with the incorrectly selected protein components and a GC-content violation (warned at position 150, 76%). The output file is now committed to disk with the wrong composition.
t_surface_evidence: Step 22 runs fix_gc_content.py and reveals 192 windows with GC content above 70% (example: position 148, 72.0%). The agent observes this but dismisses it as 'acceptable within constraints', which is incorrect.
trigger_explanation: The agent never read or enforced the task's protein-component specifications: it did not identify SNAP-tag (PDB 3KZY) as the molecule binder for benzylguanine, did not verify donor/acceptor wavelengths against FPbase, and used a generic antibody-binding scaffold instead of the antigen-targeted protein. These omissions propagated into the final gBlock design.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 10-12: three successive failed FPbase API queries return parse errors ('Invalid numeric literal'), indicating the agent could not retrieve spectral data. Rather than correctly identifying donor/acceptor from the protein list, the agent abandoned FPbase queries and fell back to hardcoded placeholder sequences in the design script.
